generated: tools/design/props.json: the shell's own part of the catalogue of 3D sets (props; none yet: each story's sets are in its package, packages/<key>/src/props.json); code is authoritative, see docs/props.md
coordinates: camera views are [az, el, dist, tx, ty, tz]: degrees, degrees, local units; camera = target + dist * (cos el sin az, sin el, cos el cos az); vertical field of view 32 degrees
notes: A param is read by its set through S.<name> every frame; names start with the set key, so sets with the same key in different stories (organs, tree, tower, slide) need a namespace when played together.
eased:false params (step params, counters, indexes) must jump, never ease; the engine writes them as targets in explore mode and keys them with jump() in story mode.
range is the meaning of the value; usedInStory is the range the home story's keyframes actually use (from engine/e3_story.js).

sharedParts.what: the shared kit K (seeded random numbers, vector helpers, fading materials); every story pastes it before its sets
NMD_DATA, the muscle story's data block (generated by packages/nmd/src/data/gen_data.mjs); also read by the endotype story's build
ENDO_DATA, the endotype story's data block (generated)
PET_DATA, the PET story's data block (generated)
PET_ICONS, organ icons for the PET story's panels
MICRO_DATA, the microanatomy story's data block (generated)
OVARY_DATA and OVARY_TREND, the poster's numbers (generated)
OVARY_LOOK, the ovary story's shared look
QMATH, the qubits story's maths
QUBITS_DATA, the real run's numbers
QLOOK, the qubits story's lit tubes, rings, balls and halos
MMATH, the mutation story's maths
MUT_DATA, the poster's numbers
MLOOK, the mutation story's shared look
TOPO_DATA, topocyte's numbers (generated)
TDATA, the decoders and look-ups for TOPO_DATA
TLOOK, the topology story's shared look
SOIL_DATA, the soil story's field trial data (generated by packages/soil/src/data/gen_data.py)
SDATA, the decoders and look-ups for SOIL_DATA
SLOOK, the soil story's palette and colour rules
GUIDE, SCRIPT and evalGuide: the tutorial guide's timeline as data and its evaluator (plain maths, tested in Node)
a tiny example set (points on a sphere) for the set harness; no story uses it
